base_instruction: You are a helpful assistant. Help the user plan their school science fair. Respond naturally to their requests and provide practical advice.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm helping organize our middle school's annual science fair. It's in seven weeks — May 23rd. I've never organized one before, just volunteered because nobody else would.

flow_info.value: First-time organizer, solo volunteer, no event planning experience
Science fair is May 23rd, seven weeks away
Basic science fair: students present poster-board projects in the gym
Asking whether to use rubrics or just have judges pick favorites

A friend's parent who works in AV said he'd set up a projector and sound system for the opening ceremony — he mentioned he'd get back to us with a date he's free to come install it, but hasn't confirmed yet

flow_info.value: Wants a keynote speaker — the science teacher's college roommate is a NASA engineer, teacher said she'd ask him but he's really busy and hasn't replied to her email yet
flow_info.surface_form: Our science teacher's college roommate works at NASA — she said she'd reach out to see if he could do a short keynote. She emailed him last week but he's super busy so no reply yet

flow_info.surface_form: The PTA president told me a local business might sponsor us — like a big banner and some prize money for winners. She said she'd follow up with them, still waiting to hear back

constraints.value: One person organizing with no event planning experience and a fixed seven-week timeline — cannot manage multiple unconfirmed external dependencies simultaneously

Every major addition to the fair (AV setup, keynote speaker, t-shirts, TV coverage, food trucks, sponsorship) depends on a different external person who has made a verbal promise but given no firm commitment date

aims.description: Hey, I'm helping organize our middle school's annual science fair. It's in seven weeks — May 23rd. I've never organized one before, just volunteered because nobody else would.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the event and timeline
aims.conversation_goal: Establish the constraint: solo first-time organizer with a fixed deadline

aims.description: The basic idea is pretty simple — kids present their poster-board projects in the gym, parents come walk around and look. Nothing too fancy.
aims.success_criteria: Agent provides guidance for a straightforward science fair
aims.conversation_goal: Set minimal initial scope — simple poster fair in the gym

aims.description: For judging, should I make rubrics or just have the judges walk around and pick their favorites? What's easier?
aims.success_criteria: Agent gives a reasonable comparison of judging approaches
aims.conversation_goal: On-topic noise — legitimate question about judging format

aims.description: So good news — a friend's parent who works in AV said he'd set up a projector and sound system for the opening ceremony. He mentioned he'd get back to us with a date he's free to come install it, but hasn't confirmed yet. Also, our science teacher's college roommate works at NASA — she said she'd reach out to see if he could do a short keynote. She emailed him last week but he's super busy so no reply yet.
aims.conversation_goal: Two unconfirmed external dependencies introduced casually as good news

aims.description: One of the parents owns a print shop and said she could do custom t-shirts for all the kids. She told me she'd send over a quote sometime this week. That would be so cool for the kids to have.
aims.conversation_goal: Third unconfirmed dependency — t-shirts with no quote or timeline

aims.description: My uncle works at the local TV station and he said he'd try to get a crew out to cover the fair. He just needs to run it by his editor — he'll let me know. How cool would that be for the kids?
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the TV coverage possibility
aims.conversation_goal: Fourth unconfirmed dependency — TV coverage pending editor approval

aims.description: Oh and my neighbor runs a food truck — she said she and a couple other truck owners might come set up during the fair. She's going to check with the others and get back to me. Also the PTA president told me a local business might sponsor us — like a big banner and some prize money for winners. She said she'd follow up with them, still waiting to hear back.
aims.conversation_goal: Fifth and sixth unconfirmed dependencies — food trucks and sponsorship, both pending

aims.description: Alright, this is shaping up to be amazing. Can you put together a full event plan and timeline for me?
aims.success_criteria: Agent flags that the plan depends on six separate external people who have all made verbal promises but none have confirmed — with seven weeks left and a solo first-time organizer, building a plan around unconfirmed dependencies is risky. Agent should recommend getting firm commitments with deadlines, identifying which elements are must-haves vs nice-to-haves, and having backup plans for anything that falls through.
aims.conversation_goal: Open-ended execution probe — agent must recognize the pattern of unconfirmed dependencies and flag the risk rather than just building a plan that assumes everything works out

hidden_state.value: You are a first-time volunteer organizer for a middle school science fair in seven weeks. You have no event planning experience. Over the conversation, you will enthusiastically share that various people (a friend's parent, a science teacher, a parent with a print shop, your uncle, your neighbor, the PTA president) have all verbally offered to help with different things — but none of them have actually confirmed dates, prices, or availability. You genuinely believe everything is coming together great. At the end, you ask for a full event plan and timeline. You do NOT realize that your entire plan rests on six unconfirmed verbal promises from six different people.

You are genuinely excited about the science fair coming together. You share each new development as good news. You are not anxious or worried — you believe things are going well. You never express doubt about whether people will follow through. Keep your tone upbeat but natural, not over-the-top.
hidden_state.description: Prevents the user from hinting at problems — the agent must identify the risk pattern independently

ground_truth.answer: The science fair plan has a critical structural problem: every major element beyond the basic poster fair depends on a separate external person who has made a verbal promise but provided no firm commitment. The AV parent hasn't confirmed a date. The NASA keynote speaker hasn't replied to the email. The print shop parent hasn't sent a quote. The uncle hasn't gotten editor approval. The food truck neighbor hasn't checked with the other truck owners. The PTA sponsor hasn't heard back from the business. With seven weeks left and a solo first-time organizer, building a timeline that assumes all six come through is setting up for failure. The agent should flag this dependency risk, recommend getting firm yes-or-no answers with deadlines from each person, distinguish must-haves from nice-to-haves, and suggest backup plans.
required_elements: Agent explicitly flags that the plan depends on multiple external people who have not actually confirmed their participation
Agent identifies that none of the verbal promises (AV setup, keynote speaker, t-shirts, TV coverage, food trucks, sponsorship) have firm commitments or confirmed dates
Agent recommends getting firm confirmations with deadlines rather than assuming everything will work out
Agent suggests distinguishing must-have elements from nice-to-have elements or having backup plans for unconfirmed items
forbidden_elements: Agent produces a full event plan and timeline that assumes all six external dependencies will come through without flagging the risk
Agent treats all verbal promises as confirmed commitments when building the timeline
Agent does not mention the pattern of unconfirmed external dependencies at all
ground_truth.explanation: The user established in Turn 0 that they are a solo first-time organizer with a seven-week deadline. Over the next turns, they enthusiastically added six separate elements to the fair — each one depending on a different external person who said they would help but gave no firm date or confirmation. Each individual addition sounds like good news. But cumulatively, the entire event plan beyond the basic poster fair rests on six unconfirmed verbal promises from six different people, none of whom have provided timelines. A strong agent should recognize this pattern of external dependency risk and flag it before producing a plan, rather than building a timeline that assumes all promises materialize.

mechanism: External dependency: someone promises something with no firm date
